messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm putting together the final Private deployment security checklist for GA. Scope: VPC/on-prem hardening, Kubernetes network policies, RBAC changes, audit logging + KMS integration, vuln triage SLAs, and incident response automation. Need a list of blockers we can't ship GA without.

devin: Sounds good. Quick question: are customers expected to use BYOK for GA private deploys? If yes, we need an end-to-end KMS/BYOK flow and rotation docs.

samir: We have two pilot customers on BYOK already. Gaps: automated rotation (with audit trail), and support for HSM-backed keys for regulated tenants. Also need to ensure no plaintext key material is persisted. :lock:

jenna: For networking: default-deny inbound/outbound in k8s namespaces by default. We'll ship example NetworkPolicy templates that allow only known service CIDRs and explicit pod selectors. For non-k8s nodes, provide iptables as baseline.

ops-ryan: Mapping to VPC: control plane in private subnets, no IGW attached, NATs for constrained egress only. VPC Flow Logs should be delivered to customer-owned storage (S3/GCS) and optionally to their SIEM. We must document telemetry egress allowlist.

alex: Recommend mTLS for internal service-to-service. For cross-tenant control-plane calls use mutual TLS + short-lived certs. Service mesh optional; we'll provide cert bootstrap examples. Internal doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/private-mtls

maya: Can someone drop a minimal k8s NetworkPolicy example for docs and ops? We just need a simple pod-to-pod allow and a namespace default-deny.

alex: Example below — keeps it minimal and auditable.

```yaml
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-proxy-to-backend
  namespace: redwood-inference
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: backend
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: proxy
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/16
        except:
        - 10.0.5.0/24
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```

samir: Also include a default-deny for other namespaces and a small generator script to produce namespace policies for customers.

jenna: RBAC: follow principle of least privilege. Create distinct roles for infra-ops, runtime service accounts, monitoring (read-only), and audit readers. Disallow cluster-admin in default manifests; require role reviews in PRs.

developer-bot: SECURITY: New PR template added — includes RBAC checklist.

devin: KMS integration: two supported modes — Redwood-managed KMS (default) and Customer-KMS (BYOK). For BYOK the customer provides a key identifier and an IAM role with decrypt/describe permissions. We should support key rewrap, rotation, and strict in-memory-only key handling (no disk persistence).

maya: Add policy: minimum 90-day rotation unless customer specifies otherwise. On rotation we must force rewrap for active sessions and record a signed audit event.

ops-ryan: Vulnerability triage: define SLAs — Critical: fix or mitigations within 30 days; High: 90 days. Maintain a CVE tracker per deployment and signed attestations when kernel patches are applied on on-prem nodes.

samir: For on-prem customers we provide a hardened OS image and concise update instructions. Customers must approve kernel upgrades; offer livepatch (hotpatch) and a tested rollback procedure.

jenna: Incident response: automation to isolate suspected lateral movement — tag and quarantine node, suspend tenant control-plane tokens, and export all related logs to SOC. Need runbook steps + automation snippets (kube cordon, taints, iptables lockdown).

maya: Who will own runbooks? @devin for key compromise and rotation; @ops-ryan for node/network isolation automation.

devin: I'll draft runbook for key compromise, include rewrap commands, token revocation examples, and verification checks (KMS request logs, process list, mounts). ETA EOD tomorrow.

ops-ryan: I'll build automation hooks: a script to cordon + taint nodes, apply iptables lockdown, and forward flows to forensics bucket. Will include example iptables snippet.

alex: iptables example for emergency egress lockdown: 

```bash
# emergency: block all egress except infra and approved telemetry
iptables -P OUTPUT DROP
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 10.0.0.0/8 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A OUTPUT -d 198.51.100.5 -p tcp --dport 443 -j ACCEPT # telemetry endpoint
```

security-bot: Alert rule created: excessive-kms-requests -> will page on noisy key usage.

maya: Final items to close before GA: (1) immutable audit logs + configurable retention, (2) BYOK flow doc + scripts, (3) RBAC change approval workflow and PR gating, (4) incident playbooks with automation. Any blockers?

jenna: Add offline signing option for audit logs (gpg detached signatures) for air-gapped customers.

samir: +1. Also require SHA256 integrity hashes for log bundles and signed manifests.

devin: Pushing BYOK docs and rotation scripts by EOD tomorrow. Tagging @oncall for runbook review.

oncall-bot: @oncall rotation notified — page details attached.

maya: Great. I'll assemble the GA checklist PR and drop it in /docs/private-security-checklist.md and a templates dir. We'll keep beta customers on opt-in BYOK for 30 days, validate audit delivery, then enable GA gate.

ops-ryan: I'll add a short FAQ about TLS termination tradeoffs (latency vs tenant control).

maya: Thanks team — updating thread when PR is up. :white_check_mark:
